title: Athymic Rat Model for Evaluation of Engineered Anterior Cruciate Ligament Grafts
protocol: Weigh and dissolve medical grade ester terminated poly (ε-caprolactone) in granule form in 1,1,1,3,3,3-hexafluoro-2-propanol to create a 10% w/w solution of the PCL polymer.
Let the solution stir using a stir plate for at least 3 hours to ensure a homogenous solution.
Prepare the electrospinning setup in a chemical fume hood with the fan on at all times.
Clean the acrylic box thoroughly with ethanol and cover all surfaces with Parafilm sheets to remove any impurities that may compromise the quality of the electrospun product.
Load approximately 3 ml of the above solution into a 10 ml syringe with a blunt ended 18 G, 1½ inch needle.
Remove any air bubbles by pushing the syringe up.
Lock solution into a programmable syringe pump.
Insert the needle through a small hole into the acrylic box while leaving about ½ inch of the needle outside of the acrylic box for attachment of the voltage source wire.
Electrospin the PCL solution to create a cuff of highly aligned PCL fibers for scaffold fabrication.
Use a 30 mm rotating lathe mandrel as the collector for the highly aligned PCL fibers.
Cover the mandrel tightly with a thin strip of aluminum foil.
Lock the mandrel into the motor on the opposite side of the box about 15 cm away from the syringe needle.
Insert the plastic hose into the vacuum port and connect to the fume hood vacuum source.
Turn on the vacuum source and cover the acrylic box with a lid.
Set the infusion rate of the programmable syringe pump to 2.5 ml/hr.
Turn on the motor to operate the mandrel at 3,450 rpm.
Attach the positive lead of the voltage source to the needle tip outside of the box using an alligator clip.
Once infusion of the PCL solution has begun, turn on the voltage source and set to a 20 kV operating voltage.
Infuse the solution for 12 min to create a homogenous cuff from 0.5 ml of the PCL solution.
Laser cut the PCL cuff to form multiple small sheets on a VersaLaser Cutter 2.3 operated at low-vacuum setting, 10.0 keV landing voltage, 6.4 mm working distance, and probe diameter of 3.0.
Plasma etch the PCL scaffolds using a plasma cleaner set to 450 mTorr vacuum and high power (29.6 W) for 30 seconds.
Bathe the scaffolds in 70% ethanol in a sterile environment.
Create a collagen coating solution by diluting Purecol collagen, 10x PBS, and 0.1 N NaOH in a ratio of 8:1:2.5 with 1:9 dilution in 1x PBS at 4 °C.
Mix the collagen coating solution thoroughly to ensure homogeneity.
Coat individual 1.5 mm x 35 mm x 150 µm scaffolds with a thin layer of the collagen solution.
Allow coated scaffolds to dry for 24 hours in a sterile environment.
Stack and affix four individual 1.5 mm x 35 mm x 150 µm scaffolds using a Krackow stitch with 5-0 Vicryl sutures to create a final 0.6 mm thick, multi-layered collagen-coated scaffold.
Induce anesthesia by placing the rat in an inhalation chamber and delivering 2% isoflurane with 2 L/min oxygen.
Confirm adequate anesthesia by applying pressure to the hind foot and evaluating for response.
Subcutaneously inject the rat with 25 mg/kg ampicillin and 0.03 mg/kg buprenorphine on a non-sterile back table.
Apply ophthalmic ointment to the eyes of the anesthetized rat.
Clip the fur from the operative hind limb.
Prep the surgical site with three alternating scrubs of chlorhexidine and 70% ethanol.
Transfer the rat to the operating table on a heated pad.
Secure the nose cone for anesthesia delivery.
Maintain anesthesia with 2% isoflurane in 1 L/min oxygen through the procedure.
Drape the rat in a sterile manner, leaving the operative limb exposed.
Confirm adequate anesthetization by lack of response to hind foot pressure.
Make a 2 cm long vertical incision medial to the knee, centered at the patella level.
Retract the skin laterally until the incision is centered over the knee.
Cut just medial to the patella with a scalpel and extend proximally and distally through the knee capsule.
Release the patella laterally by making a 1 cm vertical incision lateral to the patellar tendon.
Ensure the knee is fully extended.
Pass fine scissors under the patella from lateral to medial.
Spread the scissors to translate the extensor mechanism sideways.
While flexing the knee, translate the patella laterally to expose the inside of the knee joint.
Ensure clear visualization of the intercondylar notch and femoral condyles.
Transect the ACL and PCL in the notch using a scalpel.
Load power drill with a 1.6 mm k-wire.
Place k-wire tip on ACL origin in the intercondylar notch.
Drill superolaterally and visualize the exit point on the lateral aspect of the femur, removing any soft tissue as necessary with a scalpel.
Pass the k-wire in and out a few times to ensure clear passage for the graft.
Place the k-wire on the ACL footprint on the tibial plateau.
Drill anterolaterally and visualize exit point on the anterolateral proximal tibia.
Use scalpel to clear soft tissue as necessary so that the point where the k-wire exits the tibia is fully visualized.
Pass a shortened Keith needle through the femoral bone tunnel.
Thread the two suture ends from one end of the graft through the eye of the Keith needle.
Use the needle to pull one end of the graft through the femoral tunnel.
Repeat the previous step to pass the other end of the graft through the tibial tunnel.
Use 4-0 Vicryl suture to affix the femoral end of the graft to surrounding periosteum or other soft tissue with a figure-of-eight stitch.
Manually tension the graft with the knee in extension.
Affix the tibial end of the graft to surrounding periosteum or other soft tissue with a figure-of-eight stitch.
Use a scissor to cut off excess graft on both ends, leaving 1-2 mm on each end past the figure-of-eight stitch.
Extend the knee and reduce the patella.
Place a single figure-of-eight stitch with 4-0 vicryl to close the medial joint capsule.
Close the skin with a running subcuticular 5-0 Monocryl or Vicryl suture.
Inject rats subcutaneously with buprenorphine every 12 hours for three days postoperatively.
Check surgical site for drainage or wound dehiscence at the time of injection.
Asphyxiate rats individually in a closed CO2 chamber followed by thoracotomy at the time of sacrifice.
Harvest both the surgically reconstructed and contralateral limbs by separating at the hip joint.
Remove all soft tissue, including the posterior cruciate ligament and remnants from the disrupted native ACL, to isolate only the femur, tibia, and graft for the reconstructed limb.
For the contralateral limb, remove all soft tissue except the native ACL along with the femur and tibia by fine dissection.
Use a rotary tool such as Dremel to remove all but ¾ to 1 cm of bone from each end of the femur-graft-tibia complex.
Spray the ligamentous regions with normal saline regularly and frequently during this process and throughout biomechanical testing.
Fix each knee individually in 4% paraformaldehyde solution at 25 °C for 48 hours.
Submerge the knee in a solution of Immunocal reagent for complete decalcification.
Check individual samples daily to assess progress.
Once complete, perform sectioning.
Mount sections on slides.
Stain the sections as desired.
Secure the femur and tibia by wrapping 28 G galvanized steel wire around the epiphysis of each bone separately.
Pot the femur into a mixture of polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) bone cement.
Mix the two cement components.
Use the viscous mixture to secure the femur into the metal, completely encasing the diaphysis of the bone in the cemented pot with the epiphysis and attached ligament protruding freely.
Allow spontaneous free radical polymerization to gradually transform the mixed viscous components to a doughy material.
Wait for the material to solidify into a hardened matrix.
Pot the tibia using the same process as the femur, maintaining the knee ligament at 20° flexion.
Mount the cemented femur-graft-tibia complex onto a tensile testing apparatus.
Prepare to record load and displacement as a function of time from the beginning of tension to failure.
Pre-tension the graft to 2 N at a ramp rate of 0.5 N/min.
Test the graft to failure at a strain rate of 0.5 mm/sec.
Compute the failure load and stiffness from the generated load-displacement curves.
